During pendency of this petition, application under Sections 320 of the Cr.P.C has been filed which was registered as IA No.6334/2023 and I.A. No.6335/2023 alongwith affidavit of applicants and respondent No.1 and 2 stating therein that they have resolved the dispute amicably and now they do not want to pursue the matter any more.
This Court vide order dated 18.04.2023, had directed the parties to appear before the Principal Registrar of this Court for recording their statements and for verification of factum of compromise.
The Principal Registrar has submitted his report on 12.05.2023 itself and verified the factum of compromise.

In the cases of Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, Anita Maria Dias and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr. (2018) 3 SCC 290, Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.

sentences.text: After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and taking into account the law laid down by the Apex Court, in the opinion of this Court, continuance of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.
Moreso, the offence in question is not against the society but merely affects the victim.

Consequent upon the above said facts and that the accused applicants and the victim have amicably resolved the issue and they are permitted to compound the offences, this Court allows this MCRC with the following directions :-
Chargesheet as well as criminal proceedings of criminal case No.878/2021 (Police Station Kailaras Vs. Manoj & ors.) in respect of offence under Section 420 of IPC are quashed.
The applicants are discharged from all the charges.
Petition stands disposed of.
No order as to cost.
Let a copy of this order be sent to the concerned Police Station for information and compliance.

In the cases of Jagdish Channa & others Vs. State of Haryana & another (AIR 2008 SC 1968),
Madan Mohan Abbot Vs. State of Punjab (AIR 2008 SC 1969), Shiji Vs. Radhika & Another (2011)
10 SCC 705, and Narinder Singh & others Vs. State of Punjab (2014) 6 SCC 466, Anita Maria Dias and Anr. Vs. State of Maharashtra and Anr. (2018) 3 SCC 290, Supreme Court has laid down that even in non-compoundable cases on the basis of compromise, criminal proceedings can be quashed so that valuable time of the court can be saved and utilized in other material cases.
After hearing the learned counsel for the parties and taking into account the law laid down by the Apex Court, in the opinion of this Court, continuance of the prosecution in such matters will be a futile exercise which will serve no purpose.
Under such a situation, section 482 Cr.P.C. can be justifiably invoked to prevent abuse of the process of law and wasteful exercise by the courts below.
Moreso, the offence in question is not against the society but merely affects the victim.
